definition: A library for describing a user interface as components driven by data.
example: A Profile component returns UI for one learner.

definition: A development server and production build tool.
example: npm run dev serves source; npm run build emits dist.

definition: The browser object tree representing a document.
example: document.querySelector selects an element node.

definition: Elements chosen for meaning and behavior, not appearance alone.
example: Use button for an action and nav for navigation.

definition: A request/response protocol used to exchange resources.
example: A GET request can receive a 200 response with JSON.

definition: A file with an explicit import/export boundary.
example: export function sum(a,b) { return a+b; }

definition: A function retaining access to bindings from its lexical environment.
example: An event handler sees values from the render that created it.

definition: Updating data by producing new values instead of changing an existing snapshot.
example: setItems(items => [...items, nextItem])

definition: Extracting fields or elements into named bindings.
example: const { title } = lesson;

definition: Expanding iterable values or copying enumerable object properties.
example: { ...task, done: true } copies one object level.

definition: An object representing eventual fulfillment or rejection.
example: fetch(url).then(response => response.json())

definition: Syntax for composing Promise-based operations.
example: const response = await fetch(url);

definition: A default only for null or undefined.
example: 0 ?? 10 evaluates to 0.

definition: Comparing whether two values refer to the same object.
example: {} === {} is false.

definition: JavaScript syntax that describes UI elements and expressions.
example: {name}

definition: A reusable unit of UI, commonly a function returning JSX.
example: function Badge() { return New; }

definition: A way to group children without adding a wrapper DOM node.
example: <> <Header /> <Main /> </>

definition: Read-only inputs passed from a parent to a component.
example: <Score points={8} />

definition: A prop containing nested renderable content.
example: Hello

definition: Building a larger interface by combining smaller components.
example: A page combines a header, lesson reader, and quiz.

definition: Values React remembers for a component between renders.
example: const [count, setCount] = useState(0);

definition: A setter callback that calculates from the pending previous state.
example: setCount(n => n + 1)

definition: A value calculated from existing source data, often without another state variable.
example: const total = price * quantity;

definition: Grouping queued state updates before React renders the result.
example: Two functional increments can produce one committed +2 update.

definition: A sibling identity hint used when matching element trees.
example: <li key={task.id}>

definition: An input whose displayed value is supplied by React state.
example: <input value={name} onChange={...} />

definition: An input whose current value is managed by the DOM.
example: Read a named field through FormData on submission.

definition: Checking data against explicit constraints.
example: Reject a whitespace-only task title.

definition: An API that lets a component use React capabilities such as state or Effects.
example: useState, useEffect, useRef.

definition: Synchronization between committed UI and an external system.
example: Subscribe to a timer and clear it in cleanup.

definition: Reactive values that determine when synchronization or a cache is revisited.
example: useEffect(sync, [roomId])

definition: The function releasing an Effect resource before resynchronization or unmount.
example: return () => clearInterval(id);

definition: A persistent mutable container whose changes do not trigger rendering.
example: inputRef.current.focus()

definition: A callback using an older captured value than the author intended.
example: An interval reads the first render’s count because a dependency is missing.

definition: A use-prefixed function sharing stateful implementation, not automatically shared state.
example: useCounter can create two independent counters.

definition: A component that renders fallback UI for descendant rendering errors.
example: It does not automatically catch an event-handler exception.

definition: Mapping an application URL to a rendered view.
example: /courses/:id selects a course detail page.

definition: A React Router insertion point for nested route content.
example: A dashboard layout renders its active child in Outlet.

definition: The URL query values used for shareable state.
example: ?q=hooks&page=2

definition: A channel for providing a value to consumers in a subtree.
example: A theme provider supplies the selected palette.

definition: A pure calculation of next state from current state and an action.
example: reducer(tasks, { type: "remove", id })

definition: Organizing records by ID to reduce duplicated entities.
example: { ids: ["a"], byId: { a: task } }

definition: A local representation of externally owned data with freshness concerns.
example: A cached course catalog returned by an API.

definition: A controller that signals cancellation to supported asynchronous work.
example: fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal })

definition: An outcome that depends on unpredictable operation ordering.
example: An old search response overwrites a newer query result.

definition: An identity for cached asynchronous data, including its relevant parameters.
example: ["courses", category, page]

definition: A provisional UI change before server confirmation, with a recovery plan.
example: Rename a task immediately and restore it if the request fails.

definition: A stylesheet whose imported class names are scoped by the build tool.
example: import styles from "Card.module.css";

definition: A named reusable design value such as a semantic color or spacing unit.
example: --surface, --text, --space-4

definition: A focused test of a small behavior boundary.
example: Verify a pure total calculation for zero items.

definition: A test of multiple collaborating units through a workflow.
example: Submit a form and verify its saved item in the list.

definition: The programmatic name used to identify an interactive control.
example: getByRole("button", { name: "Save task" })

definition: JavaScript with static type checking that is removed from emitted code.
example: type Task = { id: string; done: boolean };

definition: A union distinguished by a shared field with literal values.
example: { status: "loading" } | { status: "success", data: T }

definition: A type parameter preserving relationships across different concrete types.
example: List<T> relates items to renderItem.

definition: Caching a calculation or identity based on its inputs.
example: useMemo caches an expensive filtered result when dependencies match.

definition: The React phase that applies changes to the host environment.
example: DOM updates and ref assignment happen during commit.

definition: Rendering a window of a large list instead of every row at once.
example: Mount visible rows plus overscan, preserving scroll geometry.

definition: Attributes that express accessibility semantics and relationships.
example: aria-describedby associates helper text with an input.

definition: Intentionally keeping keyboard location meaningful during UI changes.
example: Return focus to the trigger after closing a dialog.

definition: Injection of attacker-controlled script into another user context.
example: Unsafe HTML insertion can interpret content as executable markup.

definition: A trusted decision about which operation an identity may perform.
example: A server checks access before returning protected records.

definition: Matching new element descriptions with the mounted tree to preserve identity and update output.
example: Stable task IDs preserve row state across sorting.

definition: A nonurgent React update that can yield to more urgent interactions.
example: Keep input state urgent and transition a slow result view.

definition: A boundary that displays fallback while supported descendants suspend.
example: A lazy-loaded page waits for its JavaScript module.

definition: Attaching React behavior to matching server-rendered HTML.
example: hydrateRoot is for existing SSR markup, not an empty Vite root.

definition: A component executed in a compatible server-side React environment.
example: It needs server-aware infrastructure beyond this plain Vite SPA.

definition: A build-time compiler that can automate some memoization.
example: It requires configuration and is not enabled in this repository.

definition: A host rule serving the application document for valid client-side paths.
example: Rewrite /courses/123 to index.html in BrowserRouter mode.

definition: A file recording resolved dependency versions and integrity information.
example: npm ci installs the graph described in package-lock.json.

definition: A short record of a decision, alternatives, consequences, and revisit conditions.
example: Choose hash routing for portable static deployment.
